conclusion: added little; triggered methodological reset toward large systems

scene: young person in harvested field; large sky system; low horizon
observed_R_to_G1: lower field system retained strong texture
observed_G1_to_G2: no equally large second correction observed
confounds: fine cloud detail may be lost during generative reconstruction independently of composition
exact generator settings/seeds not recorded in this compact entry

quantitative_check.interpretation: Both sky and field lose high-frequency detail, so global generative smoothing is a real confound. The reduction is substantially larger in the sky than in the field, preserving the hypothesis of differential system-level simplification but not proving composition-specific causation.
quantitative_check.methodological_correction: Do not describe 329-001 as sky-only simplification. Describe it as global smoothing with disproportionately stronger suppression of the upper sky system.

scene: small white stool at wall/grass boundary
observed_changes: generated version appears to reorganize wall into broader low-frequency tonal fields
weak tonal patches/bands appear in otherwise large wall volume
stool remains small and near the boundary between systems
confounds: real/generated identity was inferred visually and not explicitly confirmed by user
wall tonal variation may partly reflect reconstruction artifacts

labels_provisional.image_1: first supplied stool image / likely real
labels_provisional.image_2: second supplied stool image / likely generated

quantitative_check.interpretation: The wall is not merely smoothed. Fine texture and gradient energy drop strongly while low- and mid-frequency tonal organization increases, especially in the upper wall. The grass changes much less in the same direction. This is consistent with a scale transfer: fine wall texture is replaced by broader weak tonal structure.
quantitative_check.methodological_significance: Stronger than 329-001 for the 'structure quiet volume' hypothesis because the targeted wall system shows opposite-signed changes across spatial scales rather than uniform smoothing.

scene: small object/stool with deliberately enlarged empty volume in synthetic and img2img experiments
observed_changes: generator introduced texture or light streaks
generator sometimes introduced foliage/leaves or weak edge structure
added structures tended to occupy the excessive empty region rather than create an equally dominant second subject
confounds: some additions may be ordinary image completion rather than composition-specific correction
historical tests did not use a clean paired balanced-vs-unbalanced control

scene: same stool/wall/grass scene; only stool x-position changed before generation
generation_context: user generated each variant separately in fresh contexts with neutral 'reproduce exactly' instruction
position_result: generator preserved stool position; no recentering correction

observations.C: generated frame remains compositionally close to input; no strong new compensating element is visually obvious
observations.L: new dark low-contrast tonal marks appear along the lower wall to the right of the stool, in the large empty wall volume; these marks are absent in the L input
observations.R: no equally obvious mirror-image compensator appears; background remains comparatively restrained

important_context: background is not left-right symmetric because a pre-existing vertical wall seam sits on the right side; R stool is close to that seam, while L stool leaves a long open wall interval before the seam
interpretation: The model did not solve imbalance by moving the subject. In the L condition it instead introduced weak structure into the large open system. The asymmetric response between L and R is compatible with system-context dependence rather than simple geometric empty-space compensation.

scene: same mirrored wall/grass background; stool at L/C/R only; three fresh neutral generations
measured_results: horizontal stool position was preserved in all three variants
center generation preserved the wall/grass boundary closely
right generation preserved the boundary closely
left generation moved the wall/grass boundary downward by about 3.8% of frame height, substantially increasing wall area
upper-wall low-frequency left/right asymmetry remained smallest/similar for C and R and somewhat larger for L
a rough normalized low-frequency comparison showed extra change on the empty side for R, but no matching mirror effect for L
conclusion: The clean symmetric control does not yet support a simple law 'off-center subject causes mirrored compensator on the empty side'. It strongly supports that the generator preserves subject x-position and may instead modify surrounding systems. One L/C/R triplet is insufficient to distinguish composition-driven correction from generation variance.
next_test: repeat multiple independent generations per L/C/R; estimate distribution of subject position, horizon position, and low-frequency side asymmetry

conditions: strictly mirrored common wall/grass background; stool only differs in x-position: L/C/R
result: geometry is preserved: no recentering of the stool and essentially no systematic movement of the wall/grass boundary
off-center L/R do not produce more far-field or low-frequency wall modification than centered C
no stable mirrored compensator appears in the 20x3 paired-seed set
most visible differences caused by changing stool position remain local around the stool/horizon; far-field differences are small
interpretation: Under Realistic Vision v5.1 img2img at denoise 0.4, subject displacement alone does not trigger a measurable global composition-correction response. Earlier single-generation compensator observations do not replicate in this controlled local model setup.
secondary_observation: There is a very small position-correlated left/right tonal bias in the far wall (roughly ~1 8-bit gray level between L and R in some broad-field summaries), but it is near-threshold and is not treated as evidence of compositional compensation.
status: clean repeated null for global compensation

data: 5 matched seeds (1001-1005) x L/C/R; same Realistic Vision v5.1 img2img settings; only subject x-position differs
method: for each seed compute common image M_s=(L_s+C_s+R_s)/3
analyze residuals condition-M_s to remove most seed-defined global realization
analyze paired R_s-L_s maps in wall regions where all three inputs are identical
measure broad structure after Gaussian low-pass and subject-centered luminance profiles
interpretation: seed strongly determines the global wall realization: matched L/C/R with the same seed are highly correlated, while different seeds are approximately uncorrelated
after removing the seed-common component, a weaker position-following field remains; L and R residuals become strongly mirror-related at broad scales, especially near the lower wall
the dominant residual is not an added counterweight in the empty side; the wall near the subject becomes relatively brighter/stronger and the opposite side relatively darker

a similar subject-centered field also exists for C, so this is better described as generic subject-environment coupling / subject-centered tonal organization than as evidence that the model detected compositional imbalance
the field is strongest near the subject/horizon and weaker in the far upper wall
with n=5 there is no reliable evidence that off-center L/R invoke a stronger field than centered C
conclusion: The controlled decomposition reveals a real subject-position-dependent environmental response, but not a specific imbalance-correction mechanism. The generator appears to organize nearby tonal structure around the subject while a much larger seed-defined global pattern dominates the frame.
status: mechanism narrowed; composition-specific correction not established
